**Given:** The smooth Lorentzian manifold, spacelike embedded hypersurface, normal and tensors in the Statement; in (d), the field equation at the selected point.

[L1] The normal and second fundamental form are smooth, $g(n,n)=-1$, $g(n,X)=0$, $K$ is symmetric, $g(\nabla_XY,n)=-K(X,Y)$ and $\nabla_Xn$ is tangential with $h(\nabla_Xn,Y)=K(X,Y)$ ([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[L2] The ambient connection is torsion-free and metric-compatible ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]], [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]); tangent vector fields have tangential bracket as proved in [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]] proof 6.1.

[L3] The operator is $R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$, and $R_{abcd}=g(R(e_c,e_d)e_b,e_a)$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=g^{ac}R_{abcd}$, $S=g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}$ and $G=\operatorname{Ric}-\tfrac12Sg$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Curvature is tensorial and is antisymmetric in its first pair and last pair of lowered slots ([[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]]).

[L4] Tangential trace, inverse metric and contractions use the usual tensor operations ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]], [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]); the normal projections of the field equation are $G(n,n)-\Lambda=\kappa T(n,n)$ and $G(n,Y)=\kappa T(n,Y)$ ([[lem-gr-constraint-projections]]).



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Induced connection.) On tangent fields define $D_XY=(\nabla_XY)^\top$, where $V^\top=V+g(V,n)n$. This defines a smooth connection on $\Sigma$ because tangential differentiation is independent of ambient extensions. By [L1], $\nabla_XY=D_XY+K(X,Y)n$ and $\nabla_Xn=AX$ with $h(AX,Y)=K(X,Y)$. Projecting the torsion identity gives $D_XY-D_YX=[X,Y]$, and restricting metric compatibility gives $Xh(Y,Z)=h(D_XY,Z)+h(Y,D_XZ)$. Thus $D$ is torsion-free and $h$-compatible. Uniqueness follows directly by solving these two identities for $2h(D_XY,Z)$: it equals $Xh(Y,Z)+Yh(X,Z)-Zh(X,Y)-h(X,[Y,Z])+h(Y,[Z,X])+h(Z,[X,Y])$. Hence $D$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, with its curvature and Ricci/scalar contractions defined in the same slot order as [L3]. [L1, L2, L3, algebra]

2.1 (Full tangential and normal curvature decomposition.) Expand $\nabla_X\nabla_YZ$ using step 1.1: its tangential part is $D_XD_YZ+K(Y,Z)AX$, and its coefficient of $n$ is $K(X,D_YZ)+X(K(Y,Z))$. Subtract the analogous expression with $X,Y$ exchanged and subtract $\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$. The tangential part is $R^h(X,Y)Z+K(Y,Z)AX-K(X,Z)AY$. The coefficient of $n$ is $X(K(Y,Z))-Y(K(X,Z))+K(X,D_YZ)-K(Y,D_XZ)-K([X,Y],Z)$. Writing $(D_XK)(Y,Z)=X(K(Y,Z))-K(D_XY,Z)-K(Y,D_XZ)$, and using $D_XY-D_YX=[X,Y]$, that coefficient is $(D_XK)(Y,Z)-(D_YK)(X,Z)$. Pairing the tangential part with $W$ yields the operator Gauss display, and replacing $(X,Y,Z,W)$ by $(Z,W,Y,X)$ yields its lowered-slot display. Pairing the normal part with $n$ multiplies its coefficient by $g(n,n)=-1$, yielding exactly (b). [step 1.1, L1, L2, L3, algebra]

3.1 (Double tangential contraction.) Choose any tangent basis $e_i$ at $p$ and complete it by $e_0=n$. Then $g^{00}=-1$, $g^{0i}=0$ and $g^{ij}=h^{ij}$. Let $U_{ij}=R_{0i0j}$ and $Q=h^{ik}h^{jl}R_{ijkl}$ in the lowered-slot convention of [L3]. Contracting the Gauss identity of step 2.1 gives $Q=S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2$: its first contraction is the intrinsic scalar by definition, its $K_{ik}K_{jl}$ contraction is $\tau^2$, and its $K_{il}K_{jk}$ contraction is $|K|_h^2$. No normal derivative enters $Q$. [step 2.1, L3, L4, algebra]

3.2 (Exact mixed contraction.) From step 2.1 in the same basis, $R_{0ijk}=g(R(e_j,e_k)e_i,n)=(D_{e_k}K)(e_j,e_i)-(D_{e_j}K)(e_k,e_i)$. First-pair antisymmetry gives $R_{i0jk}=(D_{e_j}K)(e_k,e_i)-(D_{e_k}K)(e_j,e_i)$. Therefore $\operatorname{Ric}_{0k}=h^{ij}R_{i0jk}=h^{ij}(D_{e_j}K)(e_k,e_i)-h^{ij}(D_{e_k}K)(e_j,e_i)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)_k-D_{e_k}\tau$, using symmetry of $K$ and $Dh^{-1}=0$. Since $g_{0k}=0$, $G_{0k}=\operatorname{Ric}_{0k}$. This proves the second formula in (c). [step 1.1, step 2.1, L3, L4, algebra]

4.1 (Exact scalar and Einstein contractions.) By [L3] and the two pair antisymmetries, $\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=h^{ij}R_{i0j0}=h^{ij}U_{ij}$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=-R_{0i0j}+h^{kl}R_{kilj}=-U_{ij}+h^{kl}R_{kilj}$. Hence $h^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=Q-h^{ij}U_{ij}=Q-\operatorname{Ric}_{00}$, and $S=-\operatorname{Ric}_{00}+h^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=Q-2\operatorname{Ric}_{00}$. Since $g_{00}=-1$, $G_{00}=\operatorname{Ric}_{00}+\tfrac12S=\tfrac12Q$. This proves the first formula in (c) without needing any value or normal derivative of $U$. [step 3.1, L3, algebra]

5.1 (Constraints.) Evaluate $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ on $(n,n)$ and $(n,Y)$. As $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,Y)=0$, the results are $G(n,n)=\Lambda+\kappa T(n,n)$ and $G(n,Y)=\kappa T(n,Y)$; insert steps 3.1-2.3 and multiply the first equation by $2$. The stated $j$ form follows from $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$. No global, compactness, completeness or field-equation hypothesis is used in (a)-(c), and in (d) only the pointwise field equation is used. [step 3.1, step 4.1, step 3.2, L4, algebra] ∎



In any Gaussian normal chart in which $n=\partial_0$, $g=- (dx^0)^2+h_{ij}(x^0,x)dx^i dx^j$, one has $K_{ij}=\tfrac12\partial_0h_{ij}$, $\Gamma^0{}_{ij}=K_{ij}$, $\Gamma^k{}_{0i}=h^{kl}K_{li}$, $\Gamma^a{}_{00}=\Gamma^0{}_{0i}=0$ and $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}={}^{h}\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$. Direct substitution into [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (b) gives $R^0{}_{i0j}=\partial_0K_{ij}-K_{jk}K^k{}_i$, so $R_{0i0j}=K_{ik}K^k{}_j-\partial_0K_{ij}$. The all-spatial formula is $R_{ijkl}=R^h_{ijkl}+K_{ik}K_{jl}-K_{il}K_{jk}$, and the one-normal formula is $R_{0ijk}=(D_{e_k}K)(e_i,e_j)-(D_{e_j}K)(e_i,e_k)$. These formulas use the lowered-slot order explicitly defined above. The proof does not require the construction of a Gaussian chart.

Reversing $n$ reverses $K$ and both mixed projections; the Gauss quadratic terms and $\tau^2-|K|_h^2$ remain unchanged. In particular replacing $K$ by $-K$ reverses the divergence expression, rather than leaving it invariant.

**Given:** the reduction data, the gauge conditions, and the reconstruction of the Weyl tensor from $(E,B)$.

[L1] The metric-compatible parallel frame has $h_{ij}=-\delta_{ij}$, $\epsilon_{ijk}=\epsilon_{0ijk}$, $\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$, and $\Gamma_a{}^b{}_0=\Gamma_a{}^0{}_b=-\chi_{ab}$. The projected derivative $D$ retains the arbitrary spatial connection coefficients; the independent-frame curvature uses the actual frame bracket. The curvature-Bianchi residual to be projected is $F_{jkl}=\nabla^iC_{ijkl}-\tfrac12(\nabla_kS_{lj}-\nabla_lS_{kj})$, and $q_j=\nabla_i(rU^iU_j)=qU_j$ in this acceleration-free gauge ([[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]], [[def-gr-dust-torsion-and-curvature-residuals]]).

[L2] Exact reconstruction: $C_{0i0j}=E_{ij}$, $C_{0ijk}=B_{ip}\epsilon_{pjk}$ and $C_{aipj}=-\delta_{ip}E_{ja}+\delta_{ij}E_{pa}+\delta_{ap}E_{ji}-\delta_{aj}E_{pi}$, with $l_{00}=l_{ab}\delta^{ab}/3=-1$. The Schouten components are those of [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]; constant $\Lambda$ differentiates to zero because $\nabla\gamma=0$ ([[lem-gr-dust-weyl-reconstruction-from-electric-magnetic]], [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

[L3] Curl symbol: the operator $C(\xi)$ on symmetric spatial tensors is skew-adjoint for the positive Frobenius product and has norm at most $|\xi|$ ([[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]]). $h^{ij}\mathcal L_Uh_{ij}$-type contractions satisfy $\mathcal L_Uh_{ij}=2\chi_{(ij)}$ in the acceleration-free comoving gauge. [L3]



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Electric projection.) Put $X_{ij}=\chi_{ij}$, $\theta=\chi=-\operatorname{tr}X$, and $\dot T_{ij}=(\nabla_UT)_{ij}=\partial_sT_{ij}$ for parallel-frame components. Spatial repeated indices in this step denote explicit Euclidean sums. The four lower-index connection actions in $\nabla^aC_{ai0j}$ give $\dot E_{ij}+\epsilon_{iap}D_aB_{jp}-\operatorname{tr}(X)E_{ij}+X_{ai}E_{aj}-X_{ap}C_{aipj}$; inserting [L2] makes this $\dot E_{ij}+\epsilon_{iap}D_aB_{jp}+2X_{ai}E_{aj}+X_{jp}E_{pi}-2\operatorname{tr}(X)E_{ij}-\delta_{ij}X_{ap}E_{ap}$. Also $\nabla_0S_{ji}=\kappa\dot r\delta_{ij}/3$ and $\nabla_jS_{0i}=\kappa rX_{ji}$, so the symmetric Schouten contribution is $\kappa rX_{(ij)}/2-\kappa\dot r\delta_{ij}/6$. Its Euclidean trace is $-\kappa q/2$; imposing $q=0$ or removing the trace yields $\kappa r(X_{(ij)}+\theta\delta_{ij}/3)/2$. Symmetrize the Weyl terms and use $(\mathcal L_UT)_{ij}=\dot T_{ij}-X_{ik}T_{kj}-X_{jk}T_{ik}$, $\chi_i{}^l=-X_{il}$ and $\chi^l{}_i=-X_{li}$ to obtain exactly the displayed $P_{ij}$. The derivative term is the displayed positive symmetric curl of $B$. [L1, L2, algebra]

1.2 (Transport equations (c).) The first equation is the vanishing of the time torsion in the parallel-comoving gauge: with $\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$ and $e_0=U$ the zero-torsion identity is exactly $\partial_se_a{}^\mu=-\Gamma_a{}^j{}_0e_j{}^\mu$, the displayed transport equation. The second is the vanishing of the time-curvature residual $\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0$ written in the same gauge; for tentative data the actual curvature is defined with the frame bracket, so the independent-frame curvature identity reads $R^{\mathrm{act}\,i}{}_{j0a}=\partial_s\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j+\Gamma_a{}^k{}_0\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j$, giving the displayed equation when the time-curvature residual vanishes. The third is $q=0$, with no division by $r$: $U(r)+r\chi=0$ reads $\partial_sr=-r\chi$. [L1, algebra]

2.1 (Magnetic projection.) Contract the last pair with $\epsilon_i{}^{kl}/2$. The time derivative is $\dot B_{ji}$. The spatial derivative part is $\epsilon_{ijl}D_aE_{la}-\epsilon_{ikl}D_kE_{lj}$, whose first term disappears on symmetrization. The four connection-slot contributions before contraction are $-\operatorname{tr}(X)B_{jp}\epsilon_{pkl}+X_{aj}B_{ap}\epsilon_{pkl}-X_{ak}B_{lp}\epsilon_{paj}+X_{al}B_{kp}\epsilon_{paj}$. The first two contract to $\theta B_{ij}+X_{aj}B_{ai}$. The last two contract to $-\epsilon_{ikl}X_{ak}B_{lp}\epsilon_{paj}$; interchanging dummy indices and using the symmetry of $B$ makes its symmetric part $+X_{kl}B_{pq}\epsilon_{pk(i}\epsilon_{qlj)}$. Hence the symmetric Weyl projection is $\dot B_{ij}-\operatorname{curl}(E)_{ij}+\operatorname{sym}(X^{\mathsf T}B)_{ij}+\theta B_{ij}+X_{kl}B_{pq}\epsilon_{pk(i}\epsilon_{qlj)}$. The Schouten contribution is $-\kappa\epsilon_i{}^{kj}D_kr/6$, antisymmetric in $i,j$, so its symmetric projection vanishes. Converting $\dot B$ to $\mathcal L_UB$ by step 1.1 gives exactly the displayed $Q$ with positive final double-epsilon term. No symmetry of $X$, hypersurface orthogonality or restriction on tilt was used. [L1, L2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 (Trace preservation (b).) On the algebraic extension to symmetric spatial tensors, let $t_T=h^{ij}T_{ij}$. Since $\mathcal L_Uh_{ij}=2\chi_{(ij)}$, one has $h^{ij}\mathcal L_UT_{ij}=U(t_T)+2\chi^{ij}T_{ij}$. The symmetric curl has identically zero trace: $\epsilon^{ikl}D_kT_{li}=0$ by symmetry in $l,i$. The electric matter term has zero trace. The electric coupling contractions combine to $-2\chi^{ij}E_{ij}+2\chi t_E$, giving $h^{ij}P_{ij}=U(t_E)+2\chi t_E$. For the magnetic double-epsilon term the identity $\sum_i\epsilon_{pki}\epsilon_{qli}=\delta_{pq}\delta_{kl}-\delta_{pl}\delta_{kq}$ gives $h^{ij}\chi^{kl}B^{pq}\epsilon_{pk(i}\epsilon_{qlj)}=\chi^{kl}B_{kl}-\chi t_B$. All magnetic coupling contractions therefore cancel the $2\chi^{ij}B_{ij}$ Lie contribution and yield $h^{ij}Q_{ij}=U(t_B)$. These homogeneous scalar ODEs preserve zero initial traces along every flow line, including where $r=0$; symmetry is preserved by the displayed symmetrizations. Thus the tracefree restriction of the extended system is invariant and is precisely the projected Weyl system derived in steps 1.1–1.2. [step 1.1, step 2.1, L3, algebra]

4.1 (Symmetry and positivity (d).) With the positive Frobenius product on spatial symmetric tensors, [L3] gives $C(\xi)^*=-C(\xi)$ and $\|C(\xi)\|\le|\xi|$; hence the $E,B$ block of the principal symbol is the symmetric matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with eigenvalues bounded by $|\xi|$, while all other blocks are multiples of the transport direction $U$: their symbol contributions are $\zeta(U)$ times the identity or zero. The full time matrix at a covector $\zeta$ is therefore positive definite whenever $\zeta(U)>|\zeta_\perp|$, which holds exactly for future-positive timelike conormals; the displayed $P,Q$ system with the transport equations is thus symmetric hyperbolic. [step 1.2, L3, algebra] ∎



- **Role.** Clause (d) is the hyperbolicity input for the local dust existence theorem; the residual and subsidiary equations that make the reduced system equivalent to the full Einstein-dust system are analysed in [[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].

**Given:** the data and constraints in the Statement, the fixed curvature slot convention, oriented proper tetrads and corrected reduced/subsidiary identities.

[L1] The corrected normal-frame Gauss/Codazzi equations and four constraint projections of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]; $R_{IJKL}=\gamma(R(f_K,f_L)f_J,f_I)$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{JL}=\gamma^{IK}R_{IJKL}$.

[L2] Weyl reconstruction from [[lem-gr-dust-weyl-reconstruction-from-electric-magnetic]]; the reduced transport and Weyl equations of [[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]]; and the curl symbol norm of [[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]].

[L3] The explicit residual definition and corrected F splitting and dual differential Bianchi identity of [[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]], with its corrected conservation normalization. These exact identities are the supplier premises, not its zero-initial-data vanishing conclusion.



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Admissible data and local normalization.) Locally let $\Sigma$ be a smooth oriented three-manifold with smooth positive definite metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$, smooth $\rho_{\rm mass}\ge0$, and constants $c>0,\kappa,\Lambda$. On $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$ define $\gamma(N,N)=1$, $\gamma(N,X)=0$, $\gamma(X,Y)=-h(X,Y)$. Future means positive $N$ coefficient. The original metric is $g=-\gamma$; $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_XN,Y)$. A smooth future $\gamma$-unit section $U_0$ is prescribed. Define $$\varepsilon=\rho_{\rm mass}c^2,\qquad T_0^\gamma=\varepsilon U_0^{\flat_\gamma}\otimes U_0^{\flat_\gamma},\qquad \mathcal T_0=\kappa T_0^\gamma.$$ Here $\mathcal T_0$ is the scaled Einstein right-hand side and $T_0^\gamma$ uses the energy coefficient of the dust supplier. For $G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\mathcal T_0$ the target Ricci tensor is $$J=\kappa\varepsilon U_0^{\flat_\gamma}\otimes U_0^{\flat_\gamma}-(\Lambda+\tfrac12\kappa\varepsilon)\gamma.$$ Its trace is $-4\Lambda-\kappa\varepsilon$, and $J-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_\gamma(J)\gamma=\mathcal T_0+\Lambda\gamma$. No density division occurs, including at $\varepsilon=0$; there $U_0$ remains the auxiliary gauge direction. Require the four corrected constraints for these data. Arbitrary $(h,K,U_0,\varepsilon)$ need not satisfy them. [given, algebra]

1.2 (Proper boost and full tensor transformation.) Choose an oriented local $h$-orthonormal frame $f_a$, $f_0=N$. Write uniquely $$U_0=W(N+v^af_a),\qquad W=\gamma(U_0,N)=(1-|v|^2)^{-1/2},\qquad |v|<1.$$ The explicit boosted tetrad is $$e_0=U_0,\qquad e_a=f_a+\frac{W^2}{W+1}v_av^bf_b+Wv_aN.$$ The coefficient $W^2/(W+1)=(W-1)/|v|^2$ is smooth at $v=0$. Substitution gives $\gamma(e_A,e_B)=\eta_{AB}$. The determinant is $+1$ by continuity from $v=0$ and invertibility; $e_0$ remains future. Thus the volume orientation is preserved. Additional spatial frame rotations belong to $SO(3)$ when using the same magnetic orientation. For $e_A=L_A{}^If_I$ transform the entire covariant tensors: $$R'_{ABCD}=L_A{}^IL_B{}^JL_C{}^KL_D{}^LR_{IJKL},\qquad C'_{ABCD}=L_A{}^IL_B{}^JL_C{}^KL_D{}^LC_{IJKL}.$$ The right dual is $C^*_{IJKL}=\tfrac12C_{IJ}{}^{PQ}\epsilon_{KLPQ}$. Lorentz invariance of the metric and the oriented volume tensor gives $(C')^*_{ABCD}=L_A{}^IL_B{}^JL_C{}^KL_D{}^LC^*_{IJKL}$. Then define $$E'_{ab}=C(U_0,e_a,U_0,e_b),\qquad B'_{ab}=C^*(U_0,e_a,U_0,e_b).$$ A boost generally mixes electric and magnetic parts. Separate orthogonal transformations of $E$ and $B$ are false. Invertibility concerns the full Weyl tensor; its reconstruction lemma identifies these contractions with the reduction's prescribed curvature. [given, algebra]

2.1 (Curvature construction using the corrected supplier.) Use [L1] with slots $R_{IJKL}=\gamma(R(f_K,f_L)f_J,f_I)$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{JL}=\gamma^{IK}R_{IJKL}$. It supplies six independent $R_{abcd}$ and eight independent $R_{0abc}$, including the cyclic relation. Define the six symmetric remaining entries by $$R_{0a0b}=J_{ab}+\sum_{c=1}^3R_{cacb}.$$ This is exactly $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=R_{0a0b}-\sum_cR_{cacb}=J_{ab}$. Algebraic curvature symmetries fix all other entries. The four remaining equations $\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=J_{00}$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{0a}=J_{0a}$ follow from the corrected Hamiltonian/momentum constraints. Set $S=J-\tfrac16\operatorname{tr}_\gamma(J)\gamma$, subtract its fixed Kulkarni--Nomizu term to obtain $C$, and perform the full tensor basis change above. No normal derivative of a constraint is needed. Gauss/Codazzi signs are owned by their supplier repair, not independently duplicated here. [step 1.1, step 1.2, L1, L2, algebra]

2.2 (Explicit initial connection.) Let $D^h$ be the Levi--Civita connection and $S_K$ satisfy $h(S_KX,Y)=K(X,Y)$. In tangent directions define $$\nabla_X(aN+Y)=\bigl(X(a)+K(X,Y)\bigr)N+aS_KX+D^h_XY\qquad(X,Y\in T\Sigma).$$ Differentiating $\gamma(aN+Y,bN+Z)=ab-h(Y,Z)$ verifies compatibility. Tangential torsion is zero because $D^h$ is torsion-free and $K$ symmetric. Differentiate the explicit boost to find every $\nabla_Xe_J$, hence $\omega(X)$, from $(h,K,U_0)$ and tangential derivatives. Specify $\omega(U_0)=0$ in this tetrad. Since $\mathcal V=T\Sigma\oplus\mathbb RU_0$, these values determine the entire initial connection one-form. For the comoving chart $e_0=\partial_s=U_0$, $\Sigma=\{s=0\}$, its conormal $\zeta=ds$ satisfies $\zeta(U_0)=1$ and initially $\zeta=N^{\flat_\gamma}/W$. Therefore $\zeta(e_a)=v_a$. In particular $e_a=v_aU_0+X_a$ with $X_a\in T\Sigma$, and $\Gamma_a=\omega(e_a)=\omega(X_a)$. Rest-frame spatial directions must not be conflated with directions tangent to the tilted surface. [step 1.2, given, algebra]

3.1 (Every initial zero quantity.) The torsion two-form is $\Theta(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$. Its tangential pullback is zero by the connection formula. The reduced frame transport equation imposes $\iota_U\Theta=0$, meaning $T^i{}_{0a}=0$ for every output index $i$. A vector-valued two-form vanishing on tangent pairs and on every $(U,V)$ pair vanishes everywhere because $\mathcal V=T\Sigma\oplus\mathbb RU$. Hence all $T$ vanish initially. Tangential connection curvature uses only tangential derivatives of its initial values. Corrected Gauss/Codazzi matches $R^{\rm pre}$ on all tangent direction pairs and every endomorphism slot, so the tangential pullback of $\Delta$ is zero. Reduced connection transport gives $\iota_U\Delta=0$, meaning $\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0$ for every $i,j,a$. The same two-form argument gives all $\Delta=0$. This uses reduced first jets, not a presumed Einstein development. The positive reduced time matrix below determines those jets uniquely. Density transport fixes $q=U(\varepsilon)+\varepsilon\chi=0$. Parallel gauge gives $\nabla_UU=0$, hence $q_a=\varepsilon(\nabla_UU)_a=0$ in the corrected residual normalization. No division by $\varepsilon$ occurs. The reduced Weyl equations give symmetric trace-free $P_{ab}=Q_{ab}=0$ at the initial first jet. [step 2.1, step 2.2, L2, algebra]

4.1 (Tilted differential Bianchi initialization.) By [L3], the explicit residual definition and $q_j=0$ give the identity $$\operatorname{cyclic}_{jkl}\nabla_jR^{\rm pre\,i}{}_{mkl}=\tfrac12\epsilon_{jkl}{}^pF_{prs}\epsilon_m{}^{irs}.$$ The identity uses left/right Hodge decomposition and contracted Schouten conservation. Pull back $D_\omega\Delta=-D_\omega R^{\rm pre}$ to three tangent slots. The pullback of $\Delta$ is identically zero along the slice, so its intrinsic covariant exterior derivative vanishes. Torsion pullback zero removes the exterior/covariant correction. Thus the displayed cyclic tensor vanishes on tangent triples. Contracting three tangent directions into the volume tensor gives a nonzero multiple of the normal conormal $\zeta^p$; invertibility of the endomorphism-pair Hodge map yields $\zeta^pF_{prs}=0$. This uses only tangential derivatives, and assumes no transverse derivative of constraints or residuals zero. With $P_{ab}=Q_{ab}=q=q_a=0$, the corrected split is $$F_{jkl}=2U_jP_{[k}U_{l]}+h_{j[k}P_{l]}+Q_i\bigl(U_j\epsilon^i{}_{kl}-\epsilon^i{}_{j[k}U_{l]}\bigr).$$ Here $P_a=F_{0a0}$, $Q_a=-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}F_{0bc}$, brackets have weight $1/2$, $h_{ab}=-\delta_{ab}$ and $\epsilon^i{}_{ab}=-\epsilon_{iab}$. All four component families are $$F_{0a0}=P_a,\quad F_{0ab}=-Q_i\epsilon_{iab},\quad F_{ba0}=\tfrac12Q_i\epsilon_{iba},\quad F_{bac}=\tfrac12(-\delta_{ba}P_c+\delta_{bc}P_a).$$ For $z=\zeta(U)>0$ and $w_a=\zeta(e_a)$, contract the $(a,0)$ components and take the negative half spatial dual of the $(a,c)$ components: $$zP+\tfrac12w\times Q=0,\qquad zQ-\tfrac12w\times P=0.$$ The exact matrix is $M=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}zI&X(w)/2\\-X(w)/2&zI\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with $X(w)b=w\times b$. Since $X(w)^T=-X(w)$ it is symmetric, and $$\langle(P,Q),M(P,Q)\rangle=z(|P|^2+|Q|^2)+P\cdot(w\times Q)\ge(z-|w|/2)(|P|^2+|Q|^2).$$ Timelike $\zeta$ gives $z>|w|$, hence $P=Q=0$; the four component families give every $F=0$. All initial quantities $(T,\Delta,F,q)$ required by the subsidiary theorem are therefore zero, by its explicit corrected dual identity. For reduced Weyl evolution the separately established curl bound is $\|C(w)\|\le|w|$. Its symmetric time matrix has lower bound $(z-|w|)(|E|^2+|B|^2)$, while transport blocks have factor $z$. Initially $z=1,w=v$, so the evolution bound is $1-|v|>0$, and the residual bound is $1-|v|/2>0$. These are distinct matrices. Arbitrary $|v|<1$, vacuum points and every $c>0$ remain allowed. [step 3.1, L2, L3, algebra] ∎



The normalization $\varepsilon=\rho_{\rm mass}c^2$ is an invertible constant conversion for every $c>0$. On positive-density regions the energy coefficient is exactly the density parameter of the existing dust definition. At zero density the velocity is separately prescribed and geodesic, so no division by density or free-boundary regularity is used. The orientation and tetrads are local computational choices; no global orientability or global tetrad is required.
